## Symptom

When an xdist worker dies mid-test under the integration tier's `--dist loadgroup` (`_build-and-test.yml`), the pytest run does not fail fast — it HANGS until the job-level `timeout-minutes: 60` cap. Observed on run 32585303586 job 97060825848 (hung 40+ min after worker deaths) and again on change 2115 PS1's Verified run 32587991195, where the integration-tier jobs sat in_progress long after the py3.13 default-suite job had already failed.

## Why this is its own defect, independent of the hang budget

Bug soppy-logophilic-husky (3fa7-94ba-42aa-4623) fixed what was KILLING the workers (a stale 20 s per-test budget expiring via os._exit(1) under timeout_method=thread). But worker death is only the trigger here; the hang is AMPLIFICATION: any future worker crash — a segfault in a C extension, an OOM kill, a genuinely hung test aborted by the thread watchdog — burns the full 60-minute job cap instead of reporting within seconds. Under `--dist worksteal` (the default-suite tier) xdist replaces dead workers and completes; under `--dist loadgroup` it does not recover, and the run stalls silently.

A secondary harm recorded on 3fa7: when a loadgroup worker dies, tests still queued on it are silently NOT RUN and not reported (95 collected outcomes vs 183 on the fixed tree locally), so the suite can shrink while the summary still reads plausibly.

## Suggested investigation

- Reproduce: a probe test that os._exit(1)s inside a loadgroup worker; observe whether the controller detects the death and how long the run takes to terminate.
- Candidate mitigations: pytest-xdist's `--max-worker-restart` semantics under loadgroup; a tighter integration-tier `timeout-minutes`; upstream xdist behaviour for node-down under loadgroup scheduling.
- Acceptance: a worker death in the integration tier must terminate the run (fail fast, naming the dead worker and unrun tests) rather than hanging to the job cap.
compiled_state.title: xdist worker death hangs the integration tier until the job-level timeout
